questions.question: The Red Fort is located in:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **The Red Fort** is situated in **Delhi**, the capital city of India.
 
• It was constructed by the Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** in the mid-17th century.
 
• The fort served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years, until 1857.
 
• It is an iconic symbol of India's rich history and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Red Fort is named for its massive enclosing walls of red sandstone and is a prominent tourist attraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi** is a city rich in history and has many other significant landmarks such as the Qutub Minar, India Gate, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
• Every year on **Independence Day** (15th August), the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the main gate of the Red Fort and delivers a nationally broadcast speech from its ramparts.
 
• The architecture of the Red Fort reflects a blend of Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
 
• Major structures within the fort include the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience), and the Rang Mahal (Palace of Colors).
 
• The Red Fort's design and layout influenced later buildings and gardens in Delhi, Rajasthan, Punjab, Kashmir, and elsewhere.

questions.question: Siachen in Himalayas is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**glacier**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Siachen Glacier,** situated in **the Karakoram-Himalayan region**, lies within the** eastern Karakoram mountain range,** close to the **borders of India, Pakistan, and China**.
 
• Stretching for **75 kilometers**, it ranks as the **second-longest nonpolar glacier** globally.
 
• Renowned as the **world's highest battlefield, **the Siachen Glacier gained this distinction due to its strategic location.
 
• In 1984, India launched a military operation to secure control over the glacier and its surrounding areas following attempts by the Pakistan army to occupy the region.
 
• Since then, India has maintained control over the glacier.
 
• Among the Karakoram's five largest glaciers, the Siachen Glacier sits at an average altitude of 18,000 feet above sea level, presenting a formidable and challenging terrain for military operations and exploration alike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Glaciers** are fascinating natural phenomena formed by the accumulation and compaction of snow over long periods.
 
• As successive layers of snow accumulate, they undergo a process of transformation into dense glacial ice under the pressure of overlying snow layers.
 
• The weight of this ice mass, coupled with the force of gravity, initiates the movement of the glacier downhill and outward, a process known as glacial flow.

• The property has a total area of 4.8600 ha.

questions.question: The idols of which three Gods are installed in Jagannath Temple, Puri?

• The temple also houses idols of Balabhadra (Lord Jagannath's elder brother) and Subhadra (their sister).

• The idol of Jagannath is made of wood and is ceremoniously replaced every twelve or nineteen years in a process known as Nabakalebara.

• Char Dham refers to the four holy pilgrimage sites for Hindus, which include Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, and Rameswaram.
 
• These sites are highly revered and are visited by devotees to attain spiritual salvation.
 
• The pilgrimage to Char Dham is considered a way to cleanse oneself of sins and attain Moksha (liberation).
 
 
 
• **Nabakalebara**
 
 
• Nabakalebara is a ritual that involves the renewal of the wooden idols of Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra, and Sudarshana.
 
• This ritual is performed when there are two Ashadha months in a year, which happens according to the Hindu calendar approximately every 12 to 19 years.
 
• During Nabakalebara, new idols are carved from specially chosen neem trees, and the old idols are buried in a sacred place within the temple premises.
